quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Only the very end differs, and it is short. Listen for a final stop after the hiss.
quests.explanation: You heard "lost": a quick /t/ closed the word right after the /s/. "Loss" ends on the hiss.
quests.vowelTensionRule: In a final cluster, the voicing of the last consonant changes the meaning; a voiced /d/ or /ɡ/ after a nasal or /l/ lengthens the preceding sound, while a voiceless /t/ or /k/ shortens it.
quests.mouthPosition: Close the tongue tip against the ridge at the end. For a voiced ending, keep the voice going and hold the preceding sound longer; for a voiceless ending, cut it short and stop the voice.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Two short vowels. Which one has any lip rounding?
quests.explanation: "Putt" keeps the lips neutral with a flat central vowel. "Put" rounds them gently and sounds deeper.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Listen for a hint of 'oo' colour in /ʊ/ - that is the lip rounding; /ʌ/ sounds plain and open.
quests.mouthPosition: Round your lips slightly for /ʊ/, then let them fall neutral for /ʌ/.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: The vowel is a slide in both. Focus on how long it lasts before the closure.
quests.explanation: That was "road": a slightly longer slide and a softer closure. "Wrote" is a touch shorter and closes crisply.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Ignore the final release; listen to how long the vowel is.
quests.mouthPosition: Keep the throat relaxed for /d/; tighten and stop for /t/.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Both end at the back of the tongue. Listen to the width of the vowel.
quests.explanation: "Lag" opens the jaw wide and sounds bright. "Leg" stays half open and crisper.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Both are front vowels, but /æ/ is lower. That extra openness makes /æ/ sound wider and slightly longer than the crisp, short /e/.
quests.mouthPosition: Place a finger under your chin: the jaw should drop noticeably more for /æ/ than for /e/.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: After the /ɡ/ comes a liquid. Does the tongue tip touch?
quests.explanation: The word was "glow": the tongue tip touched the ridge after the /ɡ/. "Grow" curls back without touching.
quests.vowelTensionRule: The tongue tip is forward and touching for /l/ and pulled back for /r/, even when it follows another consonant.
quests.mouthPosition: Feel the tongue tip move to the ridge for /l/.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Both are breathy stops. Is the release at the tongue tip or the back?
quests.explanation: "Can" releases from the back of the tongue and sounds hollow. "Tan" releases at the ridge and sounds brighter.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Front versus back closure, same voicing.
quests.mouthPosition: Feel where the tongue touches: front or back.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Same long vowel. Thin hiss or broad hush at the end?
quests.explanation: It was "lease": a thin, high hiss. "Leash" finishes with a broader hush and slightly rounded lips.
quests.vowelTensionRule: The lips and tongue position both differ, and together they change the colour of the noise.
quests.mouthPosition: Watch your lips: they push forward for /ʃ/.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Is there a nasal hum before the final /d/?
quests.explanation: "Sad" goes straight from the vowel to /d/. "Sand" inserts a nasal hum first.
quests.vowelTensionRule: The cluster differs at the end only: /nd/ vs /nt/, /ld/ vs /lt/. Listen for how long the nasal or lateral lasts.
quests.mouthPosition: Touch your throat: buzz continues for the voiced cluster.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Does a hiss come before the /p/?
quests.explanation: What you caught was "port": a breathy /p/ straight into the vowel. "Sport" opens with /s/ and a softer /p/.
quests.vowelTensionRule: After /s/, /p t k/ lose their puff of air, so the cluster sounds different from the plain word.
quests.mouthPosition: Keep the tongue tip near the ridge for both /s/ and the following /t/.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Same vowel. How does the hum end?
quests.explanation: In this phrase, "done" finished with the tongue tip on the ridge. "Dumb" ends with the lips closing.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Listen to the nasal tail: rounded and lip-closing for /m/, bright and tongue-based for /n/.
quests.mouthPosition: Check that your lips touch for /m/.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Both vowels are brief. Would the lips round softly or stay neutral?
quests.explanation: "Book" has soft lip rounding and a deeper vowel. "Buck" is neutral and flat.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /ʊ/ is round and deep, /ʌ/ is flat and central; both are short.
quests.mouthPosition: The jaw is a little more closed for /ʊ/ than for /ʌ/.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Same start. Hiss or buzz at the end?
quests.explanation: You heard "grace": a hiss and a slightly shorter vowel. "Graze" stretches the vowel and buzzes.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Word-final /z/ often loses some voicing, but it never loses the longer vowel before it.
quests.mouthPosition: Cut the vowel short before /s/.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Is there a /d/ after the /l/?
quests.explanation: In this phrase "feel" ended on the /l/. "Field" added a /d/ after it.
quests.vowelTensionRule: The consonant before the last sound is longer when the last one is voiced.
quests.mouthPosition: Shorten the nasal or /l/ before a voiceless stop.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Same rhythm and vowel. Does the tongue tip touch the ridge at the start?
quests.explanation: The word was "royal": the tongue curled back with no contact. "Loyal" taps the ridge.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /l/ sounds clear and light; /r/ sounds darker and slightly rounded.
quests.mouthPosition: Feel the tongue tip: contact for /l/, hover for /r/.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Long rounded vowels in both. Which one lasts longer?
quests.explanation: "Root" is shorter and finishes with a crisp /t/. "Rude" holds the vowel and ends softly.
quests.vowelTensionRule: At the end of a word, the vowel or sonorant before /d/ lasts longer than before /t/. /t/ is short and sharp; /d/ is longer, softer and partly voiced.
quests.mouthPosition: Touch the tongue tip to the ridge behind the teeth. For /t/ shorten the vowel and stop at once; for /d/ hold the vowel longer and close softly.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: One vowel glides, one is short and steady.
quests.explanation: It was "bowl": the vowel began relaxed and rounded off. "Bull" is short and steady.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /ʊ/ is a short, steady vowel with loosely rounded lips; /əʊ/ starts in the centre and glides toward /ʊ/, so it is longer and moves.
quests.mouthPosition: For /ʊ/ round the lips loosely and stop. For /əʊ/ start relaxed and let the lips close into a round as the vowel continues.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Same vowel. Which ending hisses sharply?
quests.explanation: Here, "mess" ended with a sharp hiss. "Mesh" ends with a broader hush.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /ʃ/ is a broader, lower-pitched hush made with the tongue pulled slightly back and the lips a little rounded; /s/ is a sharper, higher hiss with the tongue tip near the teeth and the lips spread.
quests.mouthPosition: For /ʃ/ round the lips slightly and pull the tongue back so the air flows over a wider channel. For /s/ spread the lips and bring the tongue tip close to the ridge behind your teeth.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Bright, wide vowel or a half-open one?
quests.explanation: "Dad" opens the jaw wide. "Dead" stays half open.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /e/ is a short mid-front vowel with the jaw only half open; /æ/ is more open and a little longer, with the jaw dropped and the tongue lowered at the front.
quests.mouthPosition: For /e/ open the jaw about halfway and keep the lips relaxed. For /æ/ drop the jaw further and spread the mouth slightly, as if beginning to yawn sideways.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: The words start alike. Does the word stop on the hiss, or does a quick extra stop follow?
quests.explanation: What you caught was "miss": the word ended on the hiss. "Mist" closes with a /t/ after it.
quests.vowelTensionRule: In a final cluster, the voicing of the last consonant changes the meaning; a voiced /d/ or /ɡ/ after a nasal or /l/ lengthens the preceding sound, while a voiceless /t/ or /k/ shortens it.
quests.mouthPosition: Close the tongue tip against the ridge at the end. For a voiced ending, keep the voice going and hold the preceding sound longer; for a voiceless ending, cut it short and stop the voice.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Does the word begin with a hiss?
quests.explanation: In the sentence, "no" started directly with the hum. "Snow" starts with a hiss before the /n/.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Adding or dropping /s/ at the start of a cluster changes the word: /sp/, /st/, /sk/ begin with a hiss that is followed by an unaspirated stop. Without /s/, the stop is aspirated and comes first.
quests.mouthPosition: Start with a clear hiss with the tongue behind the teeth, then move directly into the stop. Without /s/, begin with the stop and release with a puff.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Same vowel. Which ending is softer?
quests.explanation: That was "dug": the vowel lasted slightly longer and the closure was soft. "Duck" is shorter with a crisp /k/.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Word-final /ɡ/ is often partly devoiced in British English, so don't wait for the buzz; measure the vowel.
quests.mouthPosition: The back of the tongue rises to the soft palate in both; only the timing differs.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Stop or friction at the start?
quests.explanation: "Dan" starts with a tongue-tip stop. "Than" starts with soft voiced friction between the teeth.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /ð/ is a voiced fricative with the tongue at the teeth and continuous airflow; /d/ is a stop with a complete closure at the ridge behind the teeth. Listen for continuous buzzing versus an abrupt burst.
quests.mouthPosition: For /ð/ put the tongue tip lightly against the teeth and let voiced air flow. For /d/ press the tongue tip to the ridge behind the teeth, stop the air and release.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: The vowel and ending are the same. Which one taps the tongue tip?
quests.explanation: This time, "crowd" had a curled tongue with no contact. "Cloud" taps the ridge.
quests.vowelTensionRule: In a consonant cluster the /l/ or /r/ follows another consonant, so the difference is smaller. /l/ needs tongue contact at the ridge; /r/ needs a curled tongue tip and often shortens or devoices the first consonant slightly.
quests.mouthPosition: Say the first consonant, then for /l/ touch the tongue tip to the ridge, for /r/ curl it back without touching.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Back of the tongue or the tip for the first burst?
quests.explanation: You heard "cab": the burst came from the back of the tongue and sounded hollow. "Tab" bursts at the ridge and sounds brighter.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Listen for a brighter click (alveolar) versus a duller pop (velar).
quests.mouthPosition: Keep the tongue tip down for the velar stop.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Two short vowels again. Feel for any lip rounding.
quests.explanation: "Stud" is flat and neutral. "Stood" rounds the lips softly and sounds deeper.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /ʊ/ has rounded lips and a tongue pulled back and up; /ʌ/ has neutral lips and a central tongue. Lip rounding is the dependable cue.
quests.mouthPosition: For /ʊ/ round the lips softly and lift the back of the tongue. For /ʌ/ leave the lips relaxed and open the jaw a little more.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Same first sound. Compare the jaw opening.
quests.explanation: It was "gem": half open. "Jam" opens wide.
quests.vowelTensionRule: The difference is jaw opening. /e/ keeps the mouth half open; /æ/ opens it wide so the vowel sounds fuller and broader.
quests.mouthPosition: Start from /e/, then lower the jaw another centimetre without moving the tongue tip from behind the lower teeth - that wide sound is /æ/.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Thin hiss or broad hush at the end?
quests.explanation: In this phrase "gas" ended with a sharp, high hiss. "Gash" ends with a broader hush.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Compare the pitch of the friction: /ʃ/ is a deeper 'shh', /s/ is a bright 'sss'.
quests.mouthPosition: Say 'shh' as if asking for quiet, then smile and say 'sss'.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Where does your mouth close at the end: lips, or tongue tip?
quests.explanation: What you caught was "dine": the tongue tip on the ridge. "Dime" ends with the lips closed.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Both are voiced nasals; place of closure is the distinction.
quests.mouthPosition: Keep the lips relaxed for /n/.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Listen to the glide length before the ending.
quests.explanation: "Fade" gives the glide extra time and ends softly. "Fate" is shorter and ends crisply.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Both end on the same tongue position, but the voiced /d/ lengthens the preceding vowel while /t/ clips it.
quests.mouthPosition: Stretch the vowel before /d/; cut it short before /t/.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.textToSpeak: I like the tone of it.
quests.hint: Decide whether the word begins with a hiss before the /t/, or with the /t/ itself.
quests.explanation: Here, "tone" started with a breathy /t/. "Stone" starts with /s/ and a softer /t/.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Listen for the initial hiss: present in the /s/-cluster, absent in the plain word.
quests.mouthPosition: Hold the /s/ a moment before the stop.
